title: The satisfies operator and type-preserving literals
hook: satisfies checks that a value matches a type while preserving the narrower inferred literal type — unlike `: Type` annotation which widens. It catches typos in config objects without losing autocomplete on exact keys.

blocks.text: The **`satisfies`** operator (TypeScript 4.9+) validates an expression against a type without **widening** the inferred type. `const routes = { home: '/', admin: '/admin' } satisfies Record<string, string>` keeps literal keys `'home' | 'admin'` for autocomplete, while still erroring on `{ home: 123 }`. Compare with annotation: `const routes: Record<string, string> = { home: '/' }` widens keys to `string`. **`satisfies`** also powers exhaustiveness: `action satisfies never` in switch default branches.

entries.plainDefinition: Checks expression against type while preserving inferred narrower type.
entries.example: const COLORS = { red: '#f00' } satisfies Record<string, string>;

entries.plainDefinition: Compiler expands literal types to general types — e.g. 'home' becomes string.
Deep readonly literal inference — alternative to satisfies for frozen objects.
Keeping exact literal key/value types after validation.

blocks.text: Theme configs, route tables, Redux action maps, and i18n dictionaries need both **validation** (every value is a string) and **precision** (keys are exact literals for exhaustiveness). Annotation widens and loses key autocomplete. `as const` freezes but cannot validate against a wider interface. `satisfies` is the sweet spot — Reddit and LeetCode senior threads rank it alongside discriminated unions. C# has no direct equivalent; closest is `const` enums or source generators for compile-time checks.

blocks.title: satisfies vs as
blocks.body: satisfies validates shape without changing inferred type. as casts and can lie to the compiler.

blocks.title: Using satisfies for narrowing
blocks.body: satisfies does not narrow unions in control flow — use if/switch on discriminant.

blocks.title: Replacing runtime validation
blocks.body: satisfies is compile-time only — external JSON still needs Zod or manual guards.

blocks.text: Combine satisfies with `as const` arrays for tuple inference. Use in generic constraints: `T extends Record<string, unknown>`. satisfies on function return validates implementation against interface without widening return inference. In monorepos, satisfies on env config objects catches missing keys at build time. Limitation: cannot satisfy function types with overloads easily — use explicit return type annotation instead.

rows: No runtime check, no narrowing input
Bundle size, not for static config

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Confusing satisfies with as cast. Saying satisfies validates at runtime. Cannot compare satisfies vs annotation widening.

interviewTakeaways: satisfies validates against a type without widening inferred literals.
Annotation : Type widens; as const freezes; satisfies validates + preserves.
satisfies never in switch default — exhaustiveness without dummy assignment.
60s: Use satisfies on config objects to catch typos while keeping literal key unions. Not for runtime JSON or input narrowing.
Follow-up: combine with as const, discriminated union exhaustiveness.
commonPitfalls: Weak: "satisfies is just syntax sugar for as" — rejected; it validates without lying.
Expecting satisfies to narrow union parameters.
Strong: "satisfies checks assignability while preserving inference. Use for config tables and never exhaustiveness."

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS has no satisfies — literal shapes are unchecked until runtime validation.
C# const/static readonly fields validate at compile time but lack TS satisfies-style literal key preservation on object maps.
